gateDefectsFixed.defect: §3.3a — `lsp-ranges-finite` and `lsp-no-fabricated-ranges` asserted the SAME variable (lspFabricated, incremented only on !isFinite || line < 0), so a fromRange pointing at a DECLARATION passed both
gateDefectsFixed.replacement: `lsp-ranges-point-at-an-invocation`: each range is read back out of the caller's own file and must slice to the invoked name, be followed by `(` or preceded by `new`, AND fail a declaration test (a signature like `get(key: string)` also matches `name(`)
gateDefectsFixed.negativeCaseDetail: two planted declarations are convicted by the same predicate, including the exact live shape `get(key: string): T | undefined`
gateDefectsFixed.subsumptionArgument: a non-finite or negative line cannot slice to the invoked name, so the invocation predicate fails it; the count is still reported (lspFabricated) rather than dropped silently

gateDefectsFixed.defect: §3.3b — `mutation-caught` asserted only that SQLite accepted the UPDATE (`rowNow.ln === 42`); no check was re-run and `postFabricated` was computed then discarded by `void postFabricated`
gateDefectsFixed.replacement: the mutation must make a GATE CHECK red: after corrupting the row, the engine must serve the corrupted value (proving it reads the store) and the component's own D4 cross-check must classify the row as a disagreement (proving the corruption is visible to a check rather than absorbed)
gateDefectsFixed.verdictIs: a gate check turning false, not the database accepting a write
